explanations: alreadyEscalated is a plain array, and alreadyEscalated.includes(t.id) is a linear scan done for every breached ticket. Escalated IDs accumulate over time, so the loop becomes O(breached x escalated); with tens of thousands of each, a sweep that used to take milliseconds takes seconds of CPU and blocks the event loop. It should be wrapped in a Set, as onShift already is.

isBreached subtracts pausedMs from elapsed time: 40 - 15 = 25 minutes, which is under TARGET_MINUTES.urgent (30). Pausing applies to all priorities, and nothing prevents an urgent ticket from being paused.

Each batch is notified and then marked escalated before the next batch starts. The first batch was marked; the exception stops the loop before later batches are marked, so the next sweep re-finds and retries only those. Marking happens per batch, after notifying, and nothing blocks future sweeps.
When the assignee is not in onShift, the loop pushes { ...t, assigneeId: null }. It is still notified (not skipped), it is changed, and no reassignment logic exists in this code.
